criteria.criterion: A new file under docs/design/ describes starting the producer at dispatch, fetching the base CI result in the background and using it only at the checks, and pushing the candidate early so its CI overlaps verification; Grep for 'base' and 'CI' in it.
criteria.evidence: I read docs/design/overlap-ci-waits.md (new in the diff). Section 3 has three changes: (1) start the producer at dispatch; (2) fetch the base CI result in the background and use it only at the checks; (3) push the candidate when the producer ends and run the checks and verifier alongside its CI. 'base' and 'CI' appear throughout. How accurate this is against the code is a separate question, covered under criterion 2 and the findings.

criteria.criterion: The design has an Existing code section that reuses or extends docs/design/agent-and-build-slots.md, docs/design/per-job-main-landing.md and docs/design/continuous-landing.md, and states which of their rules change.
criteria.evidence: Section 2 has the table and names all three notes, but the rules it says will change are not in those notes and do not match the code. (a) It quotes the rule "the branch is pushed once, at landing" from per-job-main-landing.md. That note's own line 71 (and the same table row) says land_pr does an 'early-head replacement'. The code already pushes early: crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs:1949 `self.push_ci_branch(&id, &c, ctx.ui)` and :1953 `self.early_pr(...)`, with gh/early.rs:343 'athena/ci/<job id>' and land.rs:265 'the candidate that `go` pushes early'. (b) It quotes the rule "a job is dispatched only after the base's CI result is known" from agent-and-build-slots.md sections 3 and 4. Grep finds no such rule there. That note (section 2.3, line 107) calls the base CI wait only 'a candidate cause, not a measurement'. The real mechanism is take_baseline in run/checks.rs:514-528, which runs before the first producer invocation and waits up to ci_wait_s. The note never cites it.

criteria.criterion: The note cites throughput review 20261110-191047-6szm by id and states the predicted saving of 8.0 minutes per landed job (labeled an estimate) against the 2708.1 median.
criteria.evidence: Sections 1 and 5 say: '8.0 minutes per landed job (estimate)' against a median of 2708.1, citing `20261110-191047-6szm`. Both figures match evidence/records/throughput-reviews/2026-11/20261110-191047-6szm.json (expected_minutes_saved 8.0, window_median_minutes 2708.14).

criteria.criterion: The note states how the next throughput review measures the saving: which stage and median minutes per landed job it compares with the prediction after the change lands.
criteria.evidence: Section 5 makes the 'checks stage' the scoring measure and defines it as 'median minutes per landed job from dispatch to the end of the checks', while also saying the method `StageMinutes::median_of` stays unchanged. The code contradicts this. In crates/athena-core/src/status/throughput.rs:96-100 and 480-491, the checks stage is `check_minutes(j)`, the sum of measured check durations, and reused CI checks count as 0.0 s (warm-baseline-build.md 2.1; agent-and-build-slots.md 2.4 gives a checks median of 0.7 min). Landing and rebuild starts at the last invocation's end. The dispatch-to-producer gap and the producer-to-verifier CI wait are in no stage, so neither the checks stage nor the total can fall by 8.0 minutes. Item 3 does propose timestamp gaps, but only as evidence that the design was in force, not as the score. As written, the next review cannot score the prediction.

criteria.criterion: The note lists alternatives considered and risks (base CI failing after the producer ran, wasted work), with the handling of each.
criteria.evidence: Section 4 lists six alternatives, each with a reason. Section 6 lists six risks with handling, including risk 1 'Base CI fails after the producer ran' and risk 2 'Wasted work'.

criteria.evidence: The stat shows CHANGELOG.md, docs/design/overlap-ci-waits.md and docs/design/per-job-main-landing.md. Nothing changed under crates/, athena.toml, defaults.toml or the workflows. CHANGELOG.md is outside docs/design/, but it is on the expected deliverables list, which the brief makes the one statement of scope.

findings.summary: Change (3), pushing the candidate when the producer ends, already exists in the code. The note presents it as new and misstates the current rule.
findings.evidence: crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs:1946-1953 already pushes the admitted candidate to athena/ci/<job> ('so the repository's CI runs on it') and opens the early PR when verification starts. gh/early.rs:343-344 says the CI workflow runs on pushes to athena/ci/**, which answers the note's question on whether CI runs without a pull request. The wait that remains is the checks polling that run up to ci_wait_s (mod.rs:2034-2053) before the verifier starts. The design should target that: run the verifier at the same time as the routed CI wait. A careful reviewer would want the code read rather than guessed at.
findings.location: docs/design/overlap-ci-waits.md section 2 (per-job-main-landing row), section 3 item 3, section 6 risk 3, Questions item 2; docs/design/per-job-main-landing.md lines 173-174

findings.summary: The scoring method cannot measure the saving. The `checks` stage leaves out both CI waits.
findings.evidence: throughput.rs:96-100 and 480-491: checks = sum of measured check durations, and reused CI = 0.0 s. Landing and rebuild starts when the last invocation ends. The dispatch-to-producer gap and the producer-end-to-verifier gap fall in no stage and are not in the total. A simpler, correct measure: score the median dispatch-to-verifier-start gap (or the two gaps in item 3) from job.json and invocation timestamps, or add a new wait stage to StageMinutes.

findings.summary: The Existing code table attributes a made-up rule to agent-and-build-slots.md and does not cite the code that actually waits for base CI.
findings.evidence: Grep finds no 'dispatched only after the base's CI result is known' rule in agent-and-build-slots.md. Its section 2.3 calls the 911 s gap unexplained. The base wait is take_baseline in crates/athena-core/src/run/checks.rs:514-528: it runs before the first producer invocation and waits up to ci_wait_s for an in-progress default-branch run. The note defers the lookup to 'build job 1' when the code can be read now. warm-baseline-build.md and ci-routing.md, which document this flow, are not cited.

summary: The note docs/design/overlap-ci-waits.md is laid out well and cites review 20261110-191047-6szm correctly. I checked the 8.0-minute estimate and the 2708.1 median against the review record in the evidence snapshot. It also covers the base CI, the background fetch and the early push, and lists alternatives and risks. But two parts are wrong when checked against the code, and both are things the request depends on. First, the Existing code section says today's rule is "the branch is pushed once, at landing". The code already does that early push: run/mod.rs:1949 pushes the candidate to the CI branch athena/ci/<job> when the producer ends, and early_pr opens the pull request when verification starts. So change (3), the risk-3 handling and the second user question describe something that already exists. The wait that actually remains is the checks waiting up to ci_wait_s for that CI run before the verifier starts. The note also leaves the base-CI wait code to be "found by build job 1", but it is readable now: take_baseline in run/checks.rs runs before the first producer invocation and waits up to ci_wait_s. Second, the plan for how the next review measures the saving cannot work. StageMinutes.checks is only the sum of measured check durations, and a check reused from CI counts as 0.0 s. Landing and rebuild starts when the verifier ends. So neither CI wait shows up in any stage or in the total, while the note expects the checks stage to fall by about 8 minutes. Criteria 2 and 4 are unmet and there are major soundness findings, so the verdict is fail.
